# Decision 333 — `unicode.normalize` is a botopink normalizer on the four targets, its tables generated by a Zig build step; a prebuilt wasm library is a further `@External.Wasm` form, for later uses.

The example normalizes a user name before comparing it, as a rakun login form would. `"José"` with a
precomposed `é` and `"Jose\u{301}"` with a combining accent are different strings, so `==` is
`false`; under NFC both are the same text and `sameUser` answers `true`. NFD takes the composed
name apart, `74 111 115 101 769`. `ǅ` under NFKD is `68 122 780` — the compatibility letter split
into `D`, `z` and the combining caron. The three Hangul jamo compose to the one syllable `54620` (한)
under NFC, the composition computed by rule rather than looked up. Every answer comes from std's own
normalizer written in botopink over generated tables of one pinned Unicode version, so the four
targets agree for every codepoint and no host library is asked.

The decision's second half — a prebuilt `.wasm` library merged into the emitted module — is used by
nothing yet and is not shown.

Proving cells: none in this repository; the normalizer is std's (`02/97` step 16), proved by
botopink-lang's cells.
